answer: Make reputation slow, costly, and perishable. Like a glacier, trust accumulates only gradually from verified completed work, never from a signup burst. Each job is checked by randomly assigned independent peers, forming a trellis of cross-checks no operator can rig, since attackers cannot pick their auditors. Weight is anchored to a refundable stake slashed on fraud, and it decays unless refreshed by fresh verified work, so a thousand fake agents buy no influence without funding and faking a thousand real histories.
